front: How will a packet on computer A be routed across the internet to computer B in a different countries?

- computer B recalculated checksum
- received & calculated checksum compared 
- match = packet content accurate
- different = data been changed

front: Ways to manage the missing update problem

- serialisation
- timestamp ordering
- commitment ordering
- when a user starts to edit a record → exclusive lock set on record → other users cannot edit this record while lock is in place
- concept that when concurrent access to database is allowed → any transactions completed concurrently should have the same effect as if they were completed serially (one after the other)

- timestamps generated for each transaction
- database records timestamps of last read/write of records
- rules applied to determine if processing a transaction will result in loss of data integrity

→ e.g. transaction should be aborted if the last write timestamp of a record is greater than when this transaction started

- looks to optimise the order in which transactions are completed
- considers order of transactions with dependencies → ensure any conflicts are resolved
